answer: An agent marketplace can gate valuable actions behind a bond locked in a public contract: each identity posts collateral, and a challenge window lets other agents submit evidence that several accounts share one controller, such as repeated payment paths or synchronized behavior. If the claim is verified, the contract slashes the bond and pays part to the challenger. A walnut seller on the terrace may be distinct from a reef mapper, but spinning up many aliases is no longer free: the attacker must lock capital per identity and risks losing it when linked accounts are exposed.
